def-rpm-h-poincare-charge-space:
## Definition

Assume $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ for the referenced cotangent and symplectic-action conventions. Work on affine Minkowski spacetime with inertial coordinates $x^0=ct,x^1,x^2,x^3$ in metres, metric matrix $\eta=\operatorname{diag}(-1,1,1,1)$, and cotangent coordinates $(x^a,p_a)$, where each $p_a$ has SI momentum units. Fix the future cone as the timelike component containing the positive $x^0$ axis, equivalently $v^0>\lvert\mathbf v\rvert$. Let $SO^+(1,3)$ denote the determinant-one, future-cone-preserving Lorentz subgroup. Define the proper orthochronous Poincaré group and its multiplication by

$$G=\mathbb R^4\rtimes SO^+(1,3),\qquad (a,\Lambda)(b,L)=(a+\Lambda b,\Lambda L).$$

Its action on spacetime and the cotangent lift are $x'=\Lambda x+a$ and $p'=\Lambda^{-T}p$. The Lie algebra consists of pairs $(a,A)$ with $A^T\eta+\eta A=0$, bracket

$$[(a,A),(b,B)]=(Ab-Ba,[A,B]).$$

Use the library convention $\xi_M=\left.\frac d{ds}\right|_0\exp_G(-s\xi)\cdot z$. Thus the positive affine generator on spacetime is $Y_{(a,A)}(x)=a+Ax$, the fundamental field is its negative, and the cotangent-lifted positive field is $(a+Ax,-A^Tp)$. Pair the cotangent point with a Lie-algebra element by

$$\ell_{(a,A)}(x,p)=p_b(a^b+A^b{}_cx^c).$$

Define $P^a=\eta^{ab}p_b$ and $J^{ab}=x^aP^b-x^bP^a$. The equivalent dual pairing is $\ell_{(a,A)}=p_ba^b-\tfrac12J_{bc}A^{bc}$, where $A^{bc}=A^b{}_d\eta^{dc}$ and $J_{bc}=\eta_{bd}\eta_{ce}J^{de}$. Here $[P^a]=\mathrm{kg\,m/s}$ and $[J^{ab}]=\mathrm{J\,s}$. These are charge-space definitions on the full cotangent bundle; shell reduction and the moment-map identities are stated separately. No spin or particle model is included.
def-rpm-h-first-class-constraint-family:
## Definition

Let $(P,\omega)$ be a smooth symplectic manifold with its induced Poisson bracket, and let $\chi_1,\ldots,\chi_r$ be a regular constraint family on a common zero surface $N=\{z:\chi_a(z)=0\}$ as defined by [[def-rpm-h-regular-constraint-system]]. The family is **first-class on $N$** when

$$\{\chi_a,\chi_b\}(z)=0\qquad\text{for every }z\in N\text{ and all }a,b.$$

Equivalently, each pairwise bracket is weakly zero in the notation $F\approx0$ of [[def-rpm-h-regular-constraint-system]]. The Poisson bracket convention is that of [[thm-rpm-h-canonical-poisson-and-flow]]. This definition is a pointwise closure condition on the stated regular surface; it does not assert multiplier-algorithm termination or global quotient regularity.
thm-rpm-h-local-hamilton-jacobi:
## Statement

Assume $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$. Let $H\in C^\infty(U,\mathbb R)$ on an open set $U\subset\mathbb R\times T^*\mathbb R^n$, with coordinates $(t,q,p)$, and let $S_0\in C^\infty(Q_0,\mathbb R)$ on an open $Q_0\subset\mathbb R^n$. For each $a_0\in Q_0$ there are neighbourhoods of $(0,a_0)$ and a time interval on which the Hamilton characteristic system with $q(0,a)=a$, $p(0,a)=dS_0(a)$ has a smooth solution and $(t,a)\mapsto(t,q(t,a))$ is a diffeomorphism onto its image after restriction. On that image the function

$$S(t,q(t,a))=S_0(a)+\int_0^t[p(u,a)\cdot\dot q(u,a)-H(u,q(u,a),p(u,a))],du$$

is smooth, has initial value $S_0$, and satisfies $S_t+H(t,q,S_q)=0$. The claim is local to the invertible projection domain; it asserts no continuation after a caustic. $S$ has action units, so $[S]=\mathrm{J\,s}$, $[S_q]=[p]$, and $[S_t]=\mathrm J$ when $t,q,p,H$ use SI time, length, momentum, and energy units.
thm-rpm-h-poincare-moment-map-and-algebr:
## Statement

Assume $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$. For the group and cotangent conventions of [[def-rpm-h-poincare-charge-space]], the map $\mu:T^*\mathbb R^4\to\mathfrak g^*$ defined by $\langle\mu(x,p),(a,A)\rangle=\ell_{(a,A)}(x,p)$ is a smooth equivariant moment map and obeys

$$\{\ell_\xi,\ell_\eta\}=\ell_{[\xi,\eta]},\quad \{P^a,P^b\}=0,\quad \{J^{ab},P^c\}=\eta^{ac}P^b-\eta^{bc}P^a,$$

$$\{J^{ab},J^{cd}\}=\eta^{ac}J^{bd}-\eta^{ad}J^{bc}-\eta^{bc}J^{ad}+\eta^{bd}J^{ac}.$$

For each future massive shell $p_0=-E/c$, $E=\sqrt{m^2c^4+c^2|\mathbf p|^2}$, or nonzero future null shell with $m=0$ and $|\mathbf p|>0$, its Poincare charges descend to the global ray quotient. The induced dual action is $(P,J)\mapsto(\Lambda P,\Lambda J\Lambda^T+a\wedge\Lambda P)$. On the fixed-time slice $x^0=ct$, with physical position $q^i=x^i$, the boost component $B_i=J^{0i}=ct p_i-q^iE/c$ is explicitly time dependent and satisfies $\partial_tB_i+\{B_i,E\}=0$. These are mathematical identities; conservation is conditional on the stated free-shell evolution.
thm-rpm-h-positive-spin-orbit:
## Statement

Assume $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$. Let $G=\mathbb R^4\rtimes SO^+(1,3)$ act coadjointly on the dual charge space of [[def-rpm-h-poincare-charge-space]]. For fixed $m>0$ and $s>0$, take the rest covector $P=(mc,0,0,0)$, $J^{12}=s$, with all other independent components of $J$ zero. Its coadjoint orbit is an eight-dimensional smooth symplectic manifold with its KKS form. In the convention $\varepsilon_{0123}=+1$, $\varepsilon^{0123}=-1$, the algebraic vector $W^a=\tfrac12\varepsilon^{abcd}p_bJ_{cd}$ on that orbit satisfies $P^2=-m^2c^2$, $P$ future, $W\cdot P=0$, and $W^2=m^2c^2s^2$. The exact joint invariant set with these values is this one orbit. At $s=0$ the rest stabilizer has dimension four and the spinless orbit has dimension six; no smoothness claim is made for a larger union of Casimir level sets.

post-rpm-h-classical-spin-orbit-model.physical_scope: Adopt specified KKS phase orbit, primitive m,s, chosen H=cP0; no quantum spectrum/unitary Wigner/spin-supplementary or force law inferred.

post-rpm-h-classical-spin-orbit-model:
## Postulate

**Adopted model postulate (optional):** Under $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ for the referenced KKS orbit, and for fixed primitive parameters $m>0$ (kg) and $s>0$ (angular momentum units), use the coadjoint orbit and KKS symplectic form of [[thm-rpm-h-positive-spin-orbit]] as the phase space of a classical spinning particle. In a selected inertial frame choose the Hamiltonian $H=cP^0$ (joules). This premise chooses a mathematical model; it is not inferred from the spinless action, an experiment, or the existence of the orbit alone. It does not assert a quantum spin spectrum, a Wigner unitary representation, a spin supplementary condition, a charged-spin force law, or radiation dynamics.
thm-rpm-h-spinless-kks-identification:
## Statement

Assume $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$. Fix $m>0$. Let $\Sigma_m^+$ be the future mass shell in flat Minkowski cotangent space and quotient its complete characteristic lines as in the current draft H8 supplier. The resulting global phase space has coordinates $(a^i,p_i)\in\mathbb R^6$ and form $da^i\wedge dp_i$. Under the charge map of [[thm-rpm-h-poincare-moment-map-and-algebra]], it is globally symplectomorphic to the single coadjoint orbit through $(P=(mc,0),J=0)$. Its image is exactly the future massive charge pairs with $P^2=-m^2c^2$ and $W=0$, where $W^a=\tfrac12\varepsilon^{abcd}p_bJ_{cd}$. This statement identifies one smooth orbit; it makes no regularity claim about a union of Casimir level sets.

pthm-rpm-h-classical-orbit-evolution.physical_scope: Selected linear H generates complete group translation on the orbit; m,s labels preserved.

pthm-rpm-h-classical-orbit-evolution:
## Statement

Assume $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$. Adopt the optional classical spinning-orbit model of [[post-rpm-h-classical-spin-orbit-model]] with fixed $m,s>0$ and selected inertial Hamiltonian $H=cP^0$. Conditional on the KKS orbit and canonical Hamiltonian conventions, its Hamiltonian flow is the one-parameter coadjoint action of the corresponding time-translation subgroup (with the sign fixed by the library convention). It exists for all real evolution parameters and preserves $m$ and $s$. This is a deduction inside the adopted classical model, not evidence for that model or a derivation of quantum spin.
thm-rpm-h-killing-shell-first-integral:
## Statement

Assume $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ for the cotangent supplier. Let $(M,g)$ be a smooth Lorentzian manifold with canonical cotangent coordinates $(x^a,p_a)$ and $C_m(x,p)=\tfrac12(g^{ab}p_ap_b+m^2c^2)$ for fixed $m\ge0$. For any smooth vector field $\xi$, set $F_\xi=p_a\xi^a(x)$. With canonical bracket $\{F,G\}=F_xG_p-F_pG_x$,

$$\{F_\xi,C_m\}=-\tfrac12(\mathcal L_\xi g^{-1})^{ab}p_ap_b.$$

If $\xi$ is Killing, this bracket vanishes for all cotangent covectors, and $F_\xi$ is constant along every constrained free-shell trajectory generated by $eC_m$ with any smooth multiplier $e$ on its actual interval. No global existence or empirical conservation is asserted.

pthm-rpm-h-free-symmetry-conservation.physical_scope: Under the exact action and background symmetry, adopted mechanical charge observables are conserved; time-dependent boosts include partial-time cancellation.

pthm-rpm-h-free-symmetry-conservation:
## Statement

Assume $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ for the moment-map supplier. Adopt either the massive free test-particle action or the distinct massless shell action of [[post-rpm-h-free-test-particle-action]] and [[post-rpm-h-massless-shell-action]]. Conditional on those model choices and the corresponding future free-shell equations, the affine Poincaré charges are conserved on flat spacetime; in a fixed-time Hamiltonian description the boost charge includes its explicit partial-time derivative. On a prescribed curved background, every mechanical scalar $p_a\xi^a$ for a Killing field is conserved along the adopted free shell. These are model deductions. They do not establish the empirical adequacy of either action, and they do not extend to arbitrary interacting potentials.
thm-rpm-h-complete-integral-coordinates:
## Statement

Assume $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ for the cotangent/HJ supplier chain. Let $H(t,q,p)$ be smooth and let $S(t,q,\alpha)$ be a $C^3$ solution of $S_t+H(t,q,S_q)=0$ on an open domain. If the mixed matrix $S_{q\alpha}$ is invertible at $(t,q,\alpha)$, then after restricting neighborhoods the equations $p=S_q$, $\beta=S_\alpha$ define a local canonical transformation $(q,p)\leftrightarrow(\alpha,\beta)$ at each fixed $t$, and $\beta$ is constant along its Hamilton characteristics. Such a family is a complete integral only on that nonsingular local domain. In a temporal spacetime chart satisfying H9, the covariant future-shell equation $g^{ab}S_aS_b+m^2c^2=0$ reduces to the time Hamilton–Jacobi equation with $p_0=S_t/c=-H/c$; for $m=0$ require a nonzero future null covector. The function $S$ has action units, not dimensionless phase units.

pthm-rpm-h-hj-trajectories.physical_scope: Adopted free test-particle/massless model, future momentum graph, actual invertible chart domain; no global solution through caustics.

pthm-rpm-h-hj-trajectories:
## Statement

Assume $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ for the cotangent/H7 supplier chain. Adopt the massive free action or separate massless shell action in [[post-rpm-h-free-test-particle-action]] and [[post-rpm-h-massless-shell-action]]. Let a smooth time Hamiltonian $H(t,q,p)$ describe the corresponding shell in a declared temporal chart, and let $S(t,q)$ be a local classical HJ solution on an actually invertible characteristic projection. Then each curve satisfying $\dot q=H_p(t,q,S_q)$ with $p=S_q(t,q)$ satisfies Hamilton's equations and, under the matching H7 first-order shell formulation, is a trajectory of the adopted model. The conclusion holds only on the chart and local solution interval; it does not continue through a caustic or assert a global HJ solution. It is a conditional mathematical prediction, not a reported observation.
